silicon-atom.text: Net charge equals the proton count minus the electron count, multiplied by the positive elementary charge.

crystal-lattice.text: The nearest-neighbor distance is square root of three times the cubic lattice parameter divided by four. Eight atoms per conventional cell give number density eight divided by the cube of that parameter.
crystal-lattice.note: Use the same length unit throughout; 1 nm⁻³ equals 10²¹ cm⁻³.

variables.meaning: Boltzmann constant in matching energy units

energy-bands.text: Intrinsic carrier density equals the square root of the product of the two effective state densities, multiplied by the exponential of minus the band gap divided by twice Boltzmann constant times absolute temperature.
energy-bands.note: The radical covers the complete product N_C N_V. Joules may replace eV only if both E_g and k_B use joules consistently.

variables.meaning: Ionized donor density under the stated assumptions

doping.text: At equilibrium the electron–hole density product equals intrinsic density squared. In the donor-dominated limit, electron density follows donor density and hole density is intrinsic density squared divided by donor density.

pn-junction.text: Built-in potential equals thermal voltage times the natural logarithm of the acceptor–donor density product divided by intrinsic carrier density squared.

variables.meaning: Die survival probability in the Poisson model
Effective die area exposed to those defects

silicon-wafer.text: Poisson die survival is approximately the exponential of minus fatal-defect density times die area.

variables.meaning: Effective resistivity at the selected scale and temperature

copper-conductor.text: Wire resistance is approximately effective resistivity times length divided by the usable copper cross-sectional area.

dielectric.text: Parallel-plate capacitance is approximately vacuum permittivity times relative permittivity times facing area, divided by separation.

variables.meaning: Critical dimension in the selected resolution definition

lithography.text: Critical dimension equals the process factor times exposure wavelength divided by numerical aperture.

variables.meaning: Calibrated Preston coefficient for these units

cmp.text: Removal rate is approximately the calibrated Preston coefficient times pressure times relative speed.

mosfet.text: Long-channel triode current is mobility times oxide capacitance per area times width-to-length ratio, multiplied by gate overdrive times drain voltage minus half the squared drain voltage.
mosfet.note: Applicable here for strong inversion and 0 ≤ V_DS < V_GS − V_T; it is not a modern short-channel device predictor.

variables.meaning: Relative permittivity of the high-k layer

gate-stack.text: Capacitance per area equals permittivity divided by thickness. Equivalent oxide thickness is high-k thickness times the silicon-dioxide to high-k permittivity ratio.

variables.meaning: Local channel potential relative to source

channel.text: Local inversion charge per area is minus oxide capacitance per area times the remaining gate overdrive after subtracting the local channel potential.

variables.meaning: Total on-state path resistance in the selected regime

source-drain.text: Total on-state resistance is approximately the sum of channel, source access, drain access and contact contributions.

variables.meaning: Transfer length in the transmission-line model
Sheet resistance of the contacted conductor

contact.text: Uniform-injection contact resistance is specific contact resistivity divided by area. Transfer length is the square root of specific contact resistivity divided by sheet resistance.

spacer.text: Transition charge equals parasitic capacitance times voltage change. A qualitative capacitance model scales with effective permittivity and area, and inversely with separation.

finfet.text: Effective tri-gate width is approximately fin count times twice the fin height plus its top width.

gaa.text: Total gated perimeter is approximately twice the sheet count times the sum of sheet width and thickness.

variables.meaning: Effective charging events per clock period

inverter.text: Dynamic power is approximately charging activity times load capacitance times supply voltage squared times clock frequency.

nand.text: The output is the logical negation of A AND B: it is low only when both inputs are high.

flipflop.text: The clock period must cover maximum clock-to-Q delay, maximum logic delay, setup time and the uncertainty budget.

sram.text: At equilibrium, each storage-node voltage equals its inverter response to the other node voltage.

adder.latex: G_i=A_i\land B_i,\quad P_i=A_i\oplus B_i,\quad C_{i+1}=G_i\lor(P_i\land C_i)

variables.meaning: First operand bit at position i
Second operand bit at position i

adder.text: A position generates a carry when both operand bits are one. It propagates the incoming carry when their XOR is one. Outgoing carry is generate OR propagate-AND-incoming-carry.

multiplier.text: An unsigned binary product is the sum of every bit-pair product weighted by two raised to the sum of the bit positions.

variables.meaning: Matrix-product entry at row i and column j
variables.unit: product of A and B element units

variables.meaning: Valid row, column and reduction indices

mac.text: A dot product sums pairwise products. A matrix-product entry sums left-matrix row i times right-matrix column j over their shared index k.

interconnect.text: Uniform-wire resistance and capacitance each scale with length. Their distributed-RC delay scales with resistance per length times capacitance per length times length squared.

variables.meaning: Required path time under the selected constraints

clock.text: Clock frequency is the reciprocal of the period. Timing margin is the available period minus required path time.

variables.meaning: Area of placed standard cell i

standard-cell.text: Placement utilization is total placed-cell area divided by legally placeable area.

variables.meaning: Arithmetic throughput ceiling for the selected format
Useful bandwidth at the selected memory boundary

streaming-multiprocessor.text: Attainable throughput cannot exceed either arithmetic capacity or memory bandwidth times arithmetic intensity.

variables.meaning: Intensity when A and B are read once and C written once

tensor-core.text: Dense matrix work is approximately two times m times n times k. Ideal intensity divides that work by the bytes needed to read both inputs once and write the output once.

variables.meaning: Blocks permitted by the register-only budget
Register slots requested by one thread

register-file.text: Resident blocks cannot exceed the floor of available registers divided by registers per thread times threads per block.

variables.meaning: Byte-address offset within the mapped shared-memory address space
Bank index for the addressed word
Word width used by this mapping

shared-sram.text: Divide the byte address by four bytes, take the floor, then take the remainder modulo 32 to obtain the bank index.
shared-sram.note: The explicit four-byte divisor makes the original address-unit convention visible; this mapping is configuration-specific.

variables.meaning: Useful-byte fraction for the declared traffic accounting
Useful bytes in the counted transfers
All bytes physically moved for those transfers
Transferred byte rate over the same interval

l1-cache.text: Useful-byte efficiency is useful bytes divided by transferred bytes. Multiplying transferred bandwidth by that efficiency gives useful bandwidth.

variables.meaning: Average memory access time in the sequential model
Additional L2 lookup time after an L1 miss
L2 miss fraction conditional on an L1 miss
Additional service time after an L2 miss

l2-cache.text: Average access time equals L1 lookup time plus the L1 miss fraction times L2 lookup time and its conditional HBM miss penalty.

variables.meaning: Mean request time within the same boundary
Mean in-flight data amount under consistent payload accounting

on-chip-network.text: Average in-flight requests equal request rate times latency. The corresponding in-flight byte amount is approximately byte throughput times latency.

variables.meaning: Average independent requests needed in flight

hbm-controller.text: Required request concurrency is approximately target bandwidth times latency divided by useful bytes per request.

variables.meaning: Effective one-direction payload bandwidth per rank

nvlink-port.text: Ring time is approximately two times ranks minus one startup costs, plus two times ranks minus one divided by ranks times payload divided by bandwidth.

variables.meaning: Capacity of the documented logical Tensor Memory array

tensor-memory.text: The documented array has 128 rows by 512 columns with 32 bits per cell: 2,097,152 bits, or 262,144 bytes, or 256 KiB.
tensor-memory.note: Eight bits make one byte. This is the architectural array capacity, not a per-block allocation guarantee.

variables.meaning: Total two-stage pipeline time including fill and drain
Load time for one equal tile
Compute time for one equal tile

tensor-memory-accelerator.text: Pipeline time is the first load plus first compute, followed by N minus one tile intervals, each set by the slower stage.

variables.meaning: Effective charging activity per clock period

gpu-die.text: Dynamic power is approximately activity times switched capacitance times voltage squared times clock frequency.

variables.meaning: Peak interface byte rate before losses
Number of active parallel data wires
Effective bit rate on each data wire

hbm-stack.text: Peak bandwidth equals active data-wire count times effective bit rate per wire divided by eight bits per byte.

dram-die.text: Initial bit-line voltage change is the cell share of total capacitance times the initial cell-to-precharge voltage difference.

through-silicon-via.text: Via resistance is approximately resistivity times length divided by its circular conducting area.

interposer.text: Distributed-RC route delay scales with resistance per length times capacitance per length times route length squared.

variables.meaning: Potential joint sites in an ideal square array

microbump.text: The ideal joint-site count is usable interface area divided by pitch squared.

package-substrate.text: The impedance target is allowed voltage excursion divided by current-step magnitude.

variables.meaning: Temperature rise along the modeled path
Thermal resistance of that path, including any separately modeled contacts

thermal-interface.text: Bulk thermal resistance is thickness divided by conductivity times area. Temperature rise equals heat-flow rate times the selected total thermal resistance.

variables.meaning: Common heat-flow rate through the series path
Serial thermal resistance of layer or interface i

heat-spreader.text: Junction-to-coolant temperature rise is approximately common heat flow times the sum of serial thermal resistances.
heat-spreader.note: A Celsius temperature difference has the same numerical value as a kelvin difference.

coldplate.text: Transported heat equals mass flow times specific heat times outlet-to-inlet temperature rise.

host-cpu.text: Overall speedup is the reciprocal of the unaccelerated fraction plus the accelerated fraction divided by its speedup.

variables.meaning: Numerical effective DDR transfer rate expressed in MT/s
Conversion factor for two transfers per clock and MT/s to ns

ddr-memory.text: CAS timing in nanoseconds is 2000 times the CAS latency count divided by the numerical DDR transfer rate in megatransfers per second.
ddr-memory.note: Insert the rate number in MT/s, not transfers/s. This is CAS timing rather than complete CPU memory-access latency.

variables.meaning: Effective source-memory rate in the selected direction
Effective intervening-link rate in that direction

lpddr-memory.text: Remote-access bandwidth cannot exceed the smallest effective bandwidth of the source memory, interconnect and destination.

variables.meaning: Raw per-lane NRZ bit rate corresponding to 32 GT/s
Encoding payload fraction before transaction overhead

pcie-interface.text: Gen5 one-way bandwidth equals lane count times 32 billion raw bits per second per lane, times the 128-over-130 encoding fraction, divided by eight bits per byte.

variables.meaning: Message completion time in the path model

network-adapter.text: Message time is approximately fixed startup latency plus payload size divided by sustained payload bandwidth.

variables.meaning: Mean operation latency at the same boundary

nvme-storage.text: Average queue depth is approximately completed operations per second times average operation latency.

voltage-regulator.text: Ideal buck output is duty fraction times input voltage. Inductor current ripple is approximately input-minus-output voltage times duty fraction divided by inductance times switching frequency.

variables.meaning: Power dissipated inside the conversion boundary

power-supply.text: Efficiency is output power divided by input power. Conversion loss is output power times reciprocal efficiency minus one.

compute-baseboard.text: The voltage reflection coefficient is load impedance minus characteristic impedance divided by their sum.

variables.meaning: Waiting time from persistent fault onset to the next poll
Mean detection wait over uniformly distributed onset phase

management-controller.text: With uniform fault-onset phase, mean wait to the next poll is half the polling interval; the ideal wait lies between zero and one interval.
management-controller.note: The source writes a strict maximum below the interval. A continuous uniform wait has supremum Δt, so this states the intended per-event range (almost surely) rather than an unattained maximum. Actual observation/transport delays are excluded.

variables.meaning: Arithmetic work for the specified operation and format
Bytes transferred out of the device

grace-blackwell-superchip.text: Sequential GPU-path time is arithmetic work divided by attained throughput, plus incoming transfer time, outgoing transfer time and launch overhead.

variables.meaning: Useful arithmetic throughput under the declared work convention
Useful operations per byte crossing the memory boundary
Useful operations per byte crossing the network boundary

rack.text: Rack throughput is bounded by arithmetic capacity, memory bandwidth times memory intensity, and network bandwidth times network intensity; the smallest bound applies.

variables.meaning: Compute-tray count in the named GB200 NVL72 reference
GPU count per reference compute tray
CPU count per reference compute tray

compute-tray.text: In the stated reference, 18 trays with four GPUs each contain 72 GPUs. The same 18 trays with two CPUs each contain 36 CPUs.

variables.meaning: Sustained bandwidth usable by that transfer

nvlink-switch.text: Transfer time is at least payload size divided by the sustained bandwidth available to that transfer.

variables.meaning: One-hop link time in the simplified model
Signal propagation speed along the medium

cable-cartridge.text: Link time is approximately bounded below by propagation distance divided by propagation speed, plus payload bytes divided by payload bandwidth.

variables.meaning: Heat transported at the selected coolant-loop boundary

cdu.text: Heat transport equals mass flow times specific heat times the return-to-supply temperature rise.

power-shelf.text: Delivered DC power is conversion efficiency times real AC input power. Conductor heating is current squared times resistance.

variables.meaning: Comparable payload capacity of downlink i
Comparable payload capacity of uplink j

leaf-switch.text: Oversubscription is summed downlink capacity divided by summed uplink capacity, using the same direction and bandwidth convention.

variables.meaning: Traffic throughput crossing the defined cut
Usable directional capacity of crossing link ℓ
Set of links crossing the selected cut

spine-switch.text: Throughput across a network cut cannot exceed the sum of usable capacities of links crossing it.
spine-switch.note: T denotes throughput here, not time.

variables.meaning: Fraction of physical bits carrying counted payload

optics.text: Aggregate payload bandwidth equals lane count times raw per-lane bit rate times payload efficiency, divided by eight.

variables.meaning: Completed I/O rate over the selected workload
Mean transferred size per counted operation

storage.text: Average bandwidth is approximately I/O operations per second times mean bytes per operation.

variables.meaning: Usable stored energy before the separately modeled output conversion loss
Remaining conversion efficiency from that energy boundary to load

ups.text: Backup runtime is approximately usable stored energy times remaining conversion efficiency divided by load power.
ups.note: If usable energy is already measured at the load boundary, do not apply the same conversion loss again; set the remaining efficiency to one.

variables.meaning: Heat removed within the specified cooling boundary
Electrical input to that cooling boundary
All non-IT support real power within the facility boundary

cooling-plant.text: Cooling COP is heat removed divided by cooling electrical power. Facility power is IT power plus support power.

variables.meaning: Mean admitted jobs inside the selected system
Mean time each admitted job spends in the system

scheduler.text: Little’s law states that mean in-system jobs equal the admitted job rate times mean time in the system.

variables.meaning: Overall speedup with N-fold acceleration of the selected fraction
Accelerable fraction of baseline execution time

cuda.text: Overall speedup is the reciprocal of unaccelerated time fraction plus the accelerated fraction divided by its N-fold speedup.

variables.meaning: Arithmetic intensity at the selected memory boundary
Work in the declared floating-point convention

kernel.text: Arithmetic intensity is floating-point work divided by bytes moved. Throughput is bounded by the smaller of arithmetic peak and memory bandwidth times intensity.

variables.meaning: Events in the respective nonoverlapping baseline sums

compiler.text: A sequential baseline sums launch times, kernel times and transfer times without overlap.

nccl.text: Conventional all-reduce bus bandwidth is payload divided by elapsed time, multiplied by two times ranks minus one divided by ranks.

variables.meaning: Examples per microbatch per data-parallel replica
Accumulated microbatches per replica per update

parallelism.text: Global batch equals per-replica microbatch size times accumulated microbatches times data-parallel replicas.

checkpoint.text: Checkpoint save time is at least persisted bytes divided by sustained storage bandwidth.

variables.meaning: Time through the final output token of one streamed request
Number of output tokens, at least one
Mean gap between successive output tokens

serving.text: Response time is approximately time to first token plus the remaining token gaps times their mean inter-token latency.

quantization.text: Reconstruction multiplies the nearest integer to x divided by step size by that step size. Without clipping, absolute scalar error is at most half a step.

variables.meaning: UTF-8 byte count for that string

tokenizer.text: Token count is the length of the encoded token-ID sequence. Bytes per token divides the original string’s UTF-8 byte count by that token count.
tokenizer.note: The ratio requires T > 0 and is not a semantic-information measure.

embedding.latex: \begin{aligned}e_i&=\operatorname{onehot}(i)^{\mathsf T}E,\quad E\in\mathbb R^{V\times d}\\\frac{\partial\mathcal L}{\partial E_{j,:}}&=\sum_{t:\,\mathrm{token}_t=j}\frac{\partial\mathcal L}{\partial e_t}\end{aligned}

variables.meaning: Embedding table with one row per vocabulary item
Row vector retrieved for token ID i in the lookup identity
Column selector containing one at token ID i
Embedding row for vocabulary ID j
Embedding occurrence at sequence position t in the gradient sum
Token ID at sequence position t
Vocabulary or sequence indices as locally indicated

embedding.text: A one-hot row selects its embedding-table row. The lookup-path gradient for a shared vocabulary row sums gradients from every sequence position using that token.
embedding.note: The first e index names a vocabulary item; the gradient-sum e index names a sequence occurrence. The table explicitly distinguishes them. All values are model coordinates, not physical distances.

variables.meaning: Block-diagonal orthogonal rotary transform at position p
Query column vector before rotary transformation
Key column vector before rotary transformation

positional-encoding.text: The dot product of a query rotated at m and key rotated at n equals the original query dotted with the key rotated by the relative offset n minus m.

variables.meaning: Query matrix for one attention head
Additive attention mask: zero or negative infinity
Individual query/key vectors in the variance argument
Variance under the stated coordinate distribution

attention.text: Attention weights are a row-wise softmax of query–key scores divided by the square root of head width, plus a mask. Multiplying weights by values gives the output. Under the stated independent unit-variance coordinate assumptions, the unscaled dot-product variance is approximately head width.

variables.meaning: Output of the selected SwiGLU block

feed-forward.text: SwiGLU multiplies the SiLU gate projection elementwise by the up projection, then applies the down projection. SiLU is z times sigmoid of z. The three bias-free matrices contain approximately three times model width times feed-forward width parameters.

variables.meaning: Input representation over the normalized feature set
Mean of x over those features

variables.unit: same shape and coordinate units as x

variables.meaning: Residual transformation with matching output shape
variables.unit: same shape and coordinate units as x

variables.meaning: Identity Jacobian for the skip path
Jacobian of F with respect to x

residual-normalization.text: LayerNorm subtracts the feature mean and divides by the square root of variance plus stabilizer, then applies learned scale and shift. Separately, an identity residual add has Jacobian equal to the identity plus the transformation Jacobian.
residual-normalization.note: Normalization and residual addition are separate relations, not a claim that every architecture uses this combined block. Model coordinates are usually represented as dimensionless numbers.

variables.meaning: Joint or conditional model probability as indicated
Vocabulary logit for token ID i at this step

output-head.text: Joint sequence probability factors into conditional next-token probabilities. At each step the probability of a vocabulary item is its exponentiated logit divided by the sum of exponentiated vocabulary logits.

variables.meaning: Values per head for each key or value
Additional raw KV payload for one retained token in one sequence

kv-cache.text: Raw KV bytes equal two for keys and values times sequences, cached layers, retained positions, KV heads, head width and bytes per scalar. One additional token in one sequence adds the same product without sequence count or context length.

variables.meaning: Routing weight for selected expert i

variables.unit: same shape and units as y

variables.meaning: Total expert count (distinct from function Eᵢ)
Shared parameters included in this bookkeeping
Approximate parameters activated for one token

moe.text: The output sums selected expert outputs weighted by the router. Stored parameters include all experts; approximate active parameters include only the selected k experts plus shared parameters.

variables.meaning: Expected loss under the selected source mixture

training-data.text: Mixture loss is the weighted sum of expected per-example loss for each source. Sampling weights are nonnegative and sum to one.

variables.meaning: Step-t loss evaluated at the current parameters
Gradient of step loss with respect to parameters
First moment and its zero-initialization bias correction
Second raw moment and its bias correction
Step size applied to the normalized direction

variables.unit: same units as square root of v̂ₜ

variables.meaning: Positive update index for moment bias correction

loss-optimizer.text: Adam smooths gradients and their elementwise squares, corrects zero-initialization bias, then subtracts the step size times corrected first moment divided elementwise by square root of corrected second moment plus a stabilizer.
loss-optimizer.note: All squares, roots and divisions are elementwise. The two bias-correction relations are made explicit from the original assumptions. Parameter labels retain the source convention of updating θ_t to θ_(t+1).

post-training.latex: \max_\theta\left\{\mathbb E_{\substack{x\sim D\\y\sim\pi_\theta(\cdot\mid x)}}[r(x,y)]-\beta\,\mathbb E_{x\sim D}\!\left[D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left(\pi_\theta(\cdot\mid x)\,\Vert\,\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(\cdot\mid x)\right)\right]\right\}
post-training.text: Choose parameters to maximize expected reward minus a nonnegative coefficient times expected KL divergence from the reference policy.
post-training.note: This preserves the source core objective, omitting the separate auxiliary pretraining term used in some InstructGPT variants.

variables.meaning: Proposed action sampled from the policy
Supplied history or context at step t
Allowed tool execution in this sequential abstraction

tool-loop.text: Sample an action from the policy given current history, execute the permitted tool to obtain an observation, then update history with the action and observation.
tool-loop.note: These are typed state-transition relations, not physical scalar equations. Tool failures, permissions and asynchronous execution remain runtime conditions.

variables.meaning: Fitted model-size loss coefficient for the chosen count convention
Fitted data-size loss coefficient for the chosen count convention
Loss-minimizing parameter count at fixed C in this model
Loss-minimizing training-token count at fixed C in this model

scaling-laws.text: The fitted loss is a floor plus inverse-power model-size and data-size terms. With compute approximately six times parameters times training tokens, the optimal parameter and data allocations follow the stated complementary compute exponents.
scaling-laws.note: Powers use fixed numerical count conventions. Their fitted coefficients carry the corresponding normalization. This is an empirical planning model, not an intelligence law.

variables.meaning: Total independent trials, greater than zero
Plug-in standard error of the success-fraction estimator

evaluation.text: Estimated success probability is successes divided by trials. Its plug-in standard error is the square root of estimated probability times one minus that probability divided by trial count.

variables.meaning: All counted generated tokens in one sampling segment
Counted fixed input context for that segment

astra.text: Counted generated tokens include reasoning, visible output and other counted formatting. Input plus generated tokens must fit context, and generated tokens must fit the effective output cap.
astra.note: This retains the source bookkeeping abstraction and does not assert current product limits or hidden architecture. Use actual provider accounting for the specified segment.
